prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing. Create ONE finished flat opaque landscape 16:9 social-media poster for a weekend houseplant market.

Input image 1 is an original planning diagram for actual-copy scale, harmonious Korean/Latin type anatomy, two unequal repotting contact crops and a continuous reading route. Interpret its geometry rather than copying its pale gray planes or blob shapes as finished art. It is neither client artwork nor a fixed-coordinate preservation condition. Create real close photographic scenes and finished planar typography together.

Whole design: a photographic editorial contact diptych frames a central prose column. An upper left header begins with a quiet market eyebrow, then a generous dominant Korean Title, then a compact quieter English companion. The actual Korean Title is immediately recognizable as the primary typographic anchor, roughly twice the body scale. Below that header, a tall edge-bleeding crop at the left shows a healthy leafy houseplant with its attached dense rootball, supported securely from below by one clearly readable adult hand and forearm. Fine roots, crumbly soil, living stems and leaves show real plant structure; fingers visibly bear the weight with credible contact. At the right, a shorter unequal close overhead crop shows one adult hand gently steadying the rim of a real round ceramic planting pot beside loose potting soil. The thumb/fingers contact the near rim clearly and connect to one coherent wrist. These are two related views of repotting practice, not before/after images, not a chronological tutorial and not an assertion of identical plants. Photographic crop boundaries enclose the central explanation, and the shorter right crop opens into the practical rows below. Make the images substantial structural masses with close tactile contact and olive-gray tonal separation, not small decorations attached to an information template.

Central reading route: a moderately emphasized promise subtitle at the central start leads into the complete explanation in five left-aligned meaning-based lines, with generous body size and regular line spacing as in the guide. The final line descends directly on the same start axis into the date, paired with hours on its right; venue/access share the next row; care follows; invitation and URL form the last local paired row. All lines belong to this continuous body-to-participation route, not remote corner islands. Keep the last row comfortably clear of the bottom edge. Use the open area created by the unequal contact crops for these actual information rows. No added panel boxes, dividers, labels, bullets, pipes, arrows or plant tags.

Typography and finish: one mature proportional sans system close in anatomy to Apple SD Gothic Neo, with open Korean counters, stable syllable widths, semibold dominant Title, restrained semibold eyebrow/subtitle, medium prose and practical copy. Consistent baselines and optical Latin/numeral size. Body approximately the guide's reading scale (about 17px when the whole poster is 720px wide), practical lines around 15px; resolve full-copy space before increasing headline or imagery. Crisp dark charcoal-olive ink on clean warm off-white reading space. The photographs use near-monochrome restrained olive-gray grading, natural soft directional light, real skin folds, root fibres, soil grains and ceramic texture, with crisp editorial rectangular crop edges. Photographic detail stays inside the images; all type stays planar, precise, and free of image texture, shadow, distortion or perspective. Warm hands-on curiosity should express choosing a living plant and learning to care for it.

Print ONLY the following copy, each entry exactly once. Role words below describe hierarchy and are not printed. Preserve meaningful word spaces, every Korean syllable, case, ampersand, commas, periods, colons, middle dots and original en dashes. Do not replace the time/date en dash with a short hyphen; make its length clear. Soft line wraps are allowed at word boundaries; keep the paragraph's five-line meaning groups suggested by the guide.
